title: QuoteVerify: Inference-Time Quote-Backed Citation Verification for Deep Research Reports

contributions.purpose: Detect and correct hallucinated or unsupported citations in long-form research reports without retraining the generator.
contributions.mechanism: A five-stage modular inference-time pipeline (structured citation triple generation, source fetching, quote validity checking via substring matching, NLI entailment gating, repair-or-drop) that wraps any base report generator.
contributions.evaluation: Demonstrated on ReportBench as a training-free wrapper producing statistically significant citation-quality gains over standard baselines.
contributions.domain: citation verification for deep research agents
contributions.source_quote: A modular inference-time citation verification pipeline that operates as a wrapper around any base report generator, requiring no additional training.

contributions.purpose: Show that the pipeline measurably improves cited-statement match rates across models.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical evaluation on ReportBench with significance testing against standard baselines.
contributions.evaluation: Cited-statement match rate gains of +18.7pp on GPT-4o (p = 0.019) and +12.5pp on Gemini-2.5-Pro (p = 0.011).
contributions.domain: citation verification for deep research agents
contributions.source_quote: Empirical evaluation on ReportBench showing statistically significant improvement over standard baselines: +18.7pp on GPT-4o (p = 0.019) and +12.5pp on Gemini-2.5-Pro (p = 0.011).

contributions.purpose: Identify the dominant failure mode limiting quote-backed citation pipelines.
contributions.mechanism: Stage-wise analysis of pipeline success rates separating source fetching from quote validity.
contributions.evaluation: Even with 89-100% source fetch rates, quote validity remains 18-28%, indicating LLMs tend to paraphrase rather than quote verbatim.
contributions.domain: citation verification for deep research agents
contributions.source_quote: Analysis revealing that quote validity is the primary bottleneck: even for successfully fetched sources (89–100% fetch rate), quote validity remains low (18–28%), indicating that LLMs paraphrase rather than verbatim quote.

contributions.purpose: Attribute the pipeline's gains to its components.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies removing the structured citation format and the NLI entailment gate.
contributions.evaluation: Ablations show the structured citation format drives most gains while the entailment gate prevents semantically irrelevant quotes.
contributions.domain: citation verification for deep research agents
contributions.source_quote: Ablation studies demonstrating that the structured citation format drives most gains, while the entailment gate prevents semantically irrelevant quotes.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These approaches require substantial training data and model fine-tuning. In contrast, QuoteVerify operates at inference time without additional training, making it applicable to any LLM-generated report.
These works focus on evaluation metrics and benchmarks; we build on these insights but focus on verification and correction of citations at inference time.
Our work differs by specifically targeting quote-level grounding: we verify that cited evidence quotes actually appear in sources and semantically support the claims.
Inference-time verification for long-form research reports—where citations point to external documents and claims span multiple sources—remains underexplored.

notes: Paper acknowledges a core limitation as a finding: quote validity is only 18-28% even for successfully fetched sources, i.e. the mechanism's central primitive (verbatim quoting) mostly fails and gains come mainly from the structured format.
